entities.name: CGRP fiber sprouting in laminae III-IV

relationships.subject: TrkB-expressing LTMRs
relationships.evidence_quote: Taken together, only pre-injury—not post-injury—ablation of TrkB-expressing mechanosensory neurons reduces SCI-induced mechanical allodynia.

relationships.subject: spinal cord injury
relationships.evidence_quote: Therefore, a midthoracic contusion SCI induces hyperexcitability of peripheral nociceptive fibers but not mechanoreceptors of the hind paw.

relationships.subject: spinal cord injury
relationships.object: CGRP fiber sprouting in laminae III-IV
relationships.evidence_quote: Peptidergic nociceptor sprouting into lamina III/IV below injury level as a consequence of SCI was not altered by either mechanoreceptor ablation.

relationships.subject: nociceptor hyperexcitability
relationships.evidence_quote: Hyperexcitable nociceptors seem to be the main drivers of SCI-induced NP.

key_findings: Ablation of TrkB-expressing LTMRs before, but not after, thoracic contusion SCI reduced mechanical allodynia; CGRP sprouting in laminae III-IV was unaffected.

Seven days after SCI, C- and Adelta-fiber nociceptors, but not LTMRs, were hyperexcitable in skin-nerve preparations, and human SCI subjects showed lowered mechanical pain thresholds with unchanged detection thresholds.
